conditions.detail: allocator per-allocation overhead and fragmentation are not modelled
TRANSIENT_SNAPSHOTS (2, C-1 E3) and EXECUTIONS (1) are inventories by code inspection, not enforced by a counter
the main thread's stack is reserved by the platform; counted at 1 MiB because it only spawns and joins
the execution term relies on revm 19.7 behaviour checked by source inspection (iterative frames, SharedMemory truncation, fixed stack capacity) and by measured adversarial peaks
CPU costs (world-root rebuild, chain scans, pool re-execution, deep-fork rebuild) are not memory terms; worst-case timing is not bounded

a diff keeps no storage for a removed account: under Cancun (revm 19.7, EIP-6780) only an account created in the same transaction is destroyed, and an account without code, nonce and balance holds no storage; by inspection, not enforced by a counter
the history.redb terms rely on redb 2.6.4 behaviour checked by source inspection (cache split and write-buffer flush, allocator bitmaps) and on a measured file-size factor (HISTORY_FILE_FACTOR)

Node::open holds the whole journal's payloads (store::open, pre-existing) and a replay index of two entries per record while replaying; this open-time transient grows with the journal and is not part of the steady-state bound. C-1 E4.4 adds to it, at open only: every record's offset and rolling hash, a decoded checkpoint snapshot and the stored versions read whole for their summaries (streamed: a node at a time, the DFS stack of node ids)

store mode (C-1 E4): BATCHES (1) and stored_versions are inventories by code inspection, not enforced by a counter; the node cache is bounded by its resident-byte count (state_store::CACHE_ENTRY, Node::resident_bytes), checked by a test

the pool layer, overlay and store-mode code terms rely on revm 19.7 behaviour checked by source inspection (A13-DERIVATION §2d): a touch needs paid gas or a warm address, a touch or write in a reverted frame is undone, a loaded account or slot stays until its transaction ends; that a created account keeps the slots it loaded in out-of-gas frames is also tested

the state.redb allocator term takes the largest file as STATE_FILE_FACTOR times the stored bytes: a factor measured on stores of 1.5 to 15 MB (evidence/c1-e4 disk measurements), not established for the terabyte files of the adversarial case (every version a whole state on disk)
